agent_notes: The superscription is counted as part of verse 1 in the Hebrew (KJV 125:0 and 125:1), so the word table opens with 'song of the ascents'. I translated it in the literal layer and let the dramatic layer carry it as a spoken heading.

STEPBible glosses 'yishev' as 'it will remain'. I kept 'sits/dwells' in the literal layer because the root yashav is the ordinary verb 'to sit, dwell', and the contrast with the shaken mountain depends on it. The English versions all say 'abideth'.

agent_notes: STEPBible glosses 'et' as 'with'. Here it is the preposition 'et' (with), not the object marker, so I glossed it 'with' and not [obj]. The Hebrew 'et' after hālak (hiphil) is read as 'with' by Ibn Ezra and most translators, which gives 'lead them away with the workers of iniquity'.

The sentence 'peace upon Israel' has no verb in the Hebrew. It can be a wish or a statement. I chose a wish in the dramatic layer and left the literal layer verbless, so both readings stay open. The five English versions split between 'shall be' (KJV, Webster) and a plain or optative reading (YLT, BBE).

history.note: [should_fix] Delete the sentence claiming the KJV softens the preposition; if you keep a remark on 'et', say that the KJV, like this translation, reads it as 'with' (sharing the evildoers' fate), not as the object marker. (PS.125.5: Hebrew 'et po'alei ha'aven', glossed 'with the doers of'; KJV: "the Lord shall lead them forth with the workers of iniquity")
